title: Rheumatoid factor (RF)

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: A rheumatoid factor test checks the blood for rheumatoid factor, a protein made by the immune system. It is used with other tests to help look into rheumatoid arthritis and some other conditions.
context: Many people have small amounts of rheumatoid factor and are healthy, and even higher amounts are not always a sign of a health condition. The test alone cannot make a diagnosis, and results are considered with symptoms and other tests.
aboveRange: A higher (positive) level can be associated with rheumatoid arthritis or other autoimmune conditions
May be associated with a chronic infection
May be associated with certain cancers
Some people with higher levels do not have any related condition
belowRange: A low or negative result means little or no rheumatoid factor was found, but it does not rule out rheumatoid arthritis or another condition
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
